questions.q: Anisole is treated with acetyl chloride and AlCl₃. The major product is:
questions.explain: –OCH₃ is an ortho/para director and the bulky acyl group goes mainly to the para position. Meta substitution would need a deactivating group.

questions.q: Which compound does NOT undergo Friedel–Crafts acylation with CH₃COCl/AlCl₃?
questions.explain: –NO₂ strongly deactivates the ring, and the acylium ion is too weak an electrophile to attack it; nitrobenzene is even used as a solvent for such reactions. Thiophene is acylated at C-2 under milder SnCl₄ catalysis.

questions.q: Why must at least one full equivalent of AlCl₃ be used in Friedel–Crafts acylation, whereas a catalytic amount serves in alkylation?
options: The acylium ion rearranges unless excess AlCl₃ is present
Excess AlCl₃ is needed to prevent polyacylation
AlCl₃ is consumed by the HCl formed
The ketone product is a Lewis base and binds AlCl₃, which is released only on aqueous work-up
questions.explain: The carbonyl oxygen of the aryl ketone complexes AlCl₃, so it is not regenerated at the end; water at work-up frees the ketone. Polyacylation does not occur anyway because the ketone deactivates the ring.

questions.q: Benzene is treated with pivaloyl chloride, (CH₃)₃C–COCl, and AlCl₃. The major organic product is:
questions.explain: The pivaloyl acylium ion is in equilibrium with the very stable tert-butyl cation and CO, so the ring is alkylated instead of acylated. The trap is writing the expected ketone; always check whether the carbon next to C=O is tertiary.
